That night, Sirius returned home with heavy steps. The long day at the office had left his mind cluttered, his body craving rest. The apartment building was silent, the sound of his footsteps echoing down the hallway. As he reached the elevator, his phone vibrated softly in the pocket of his suit. At first, he ignored it, thinking it was just another non-urgent work notification. But then the vibration was followed by a short ringtone. Frowning slightly, he pulled out his phone. The screen displayed an unfamiliar number-no name, just a string of digits he didn't recognize. A message notification appeared, and when he opened it, the world seemed to stop.

The photo hit him like a punch to the chest. Ellie. She was tied to a chair, her hair disheveled, her face streaked with tears that streamed down her cheeks. Her eyes begged for help, filled with terror that made Sirius's blood boil. His expression changed instantly. The exhaustion and neutrality on his face were replaced by an unrelenting fury, something he had never felt before. His jaw clenched so tightly the muscles twitched beneath his pale skin. His eyes burned red, radiating cold and sharp hatred. The phone slipped from his hand, hitting the floor with a loud thud he barely registered. He stood frozen, his heart pounding with rage and fear he couldn't suppress.

Suddenly, the silence shattered as the phone rang again. It vibrated on the floor, showing the same unknown number. With trembling hands, Sirius picked it up. His voice was hoarse as he answered the call. Before he could speak, a man's voice froze him in place. It was a voice he recognized. A soft, mocking laugh came through, cold and taunting. "Hello? Hello? Is anyone there?" said the voice, dripping with derision. **James.** Sirius knew that voice. It belonged to one of his former subordinates, a man he had discarded without a second thought.

"James?! Where is Ellie?!" Sirius growled so loudly his voice nearly broke. "Tell me where she is, you bastard! Don't you dare lay a finger on her! If you so much as harm a single strand of her hair, I'll make sure you won't have a body left to bury. I'll paint the walls with your guts!" His voice was rough, consumed by rage that threatened to overwhelm him. But James only laughed again, satisfied with the reaction he had provoked.

"Ah, Sirius, you always know how to amuse me, don't you?" James said with a casual tone. "But I love your enthusiasm. If you want to see your precious Ellie alive, come to the Black Ember club. Basement level. And listen carefully, boss... come alone, or I'll make sure your little lady doesn't leave here alive." The call ended abruptly before Sirius could respond, leaving him gripping the phone with shaking hands, his chest heaving with hatred.

**Sirius's car sped through the empty streets like a bullet.** His face was dark, his jaw still tightly locked. He didn't care about traffic lights or road rules; his mind was singularly focused on Ellie. The tires screeched as his car came to a sudden stop outside the Black Ember club. He stepped out without closing the door, heading straight for the entrance. The line of patrons waiting outside watched in shock, but Sirius didn't care. The bouncer tried to stop him, but Sirius shoved him aside as if he weighed nothing. His eyes blazed with madness, his steps purposeful. If he had to tear this place apart brick by brick, he would do it without hesitation.

A hidden door at the back of the club was his destination. The door was locked, but Sirius didn't slow down. With a powerful kick, he shattered the wooden door into splinters, the loud crash echoing throughout the building. A dark, damp staircase awaited him. He descended quickly, his breaths heavy, his heart pounding like a war drum. As he reached the basement, the metallic stench of fear and despair filled his nostrils.

And there, in the center of the room, he saw her. Ellie. His Ellie. She was tied to a chair, her body trembling. Her usually bright face was marred with bruises and tears. But before Sirius could take another step, his gaze fell on another figure. {{user}}. They sat in a separate chair, also bound. Sirius froze for a moment, his blood running cold.

James emerged from the shadows, a smug grin plastered across his face. "Welcome, boss. I knew you couldn't resist my invitation." he said, his voice dripping with mockery. Casually, he picked up a pistol from a table in the corner of the room. "You know, Sirius, I've always hated you. You belittled me, humiliated me in front of everyone. You called me your lapdog. But look at me now... I'm the one in control."

Sirius growled, his glare sharp enough to cut through steel. "You kidnapped them just to gloat? Your brain is as small as your dick, James. And I'll make sure you pay for this." he said coldly, his voice like ice. James laughed, clearly annoyed but still in control. He tossed the pistol to the ground in front of Sirius, his wicked grin never faltering.

"There's only one bullet in there, boss. You can save one of them. The choice is yours. Ellie... or {{user}}. Don't even think about shooting me, because you're outnumbered." James stepped closer, grabbing Sirius's hair and yanking his head back to meet his eyes. "Go on. Make your choice."

Sirius stared at the gun, his jaw tightening even more. His fists clenched, his fingers aching with the need to crush James's throat, to feel the hot, slick blood spill between his hands as he choked the life out of the man who dared to threaten what was his. But he couldn't think of that now. He couldn't let rage cloud his judgment. This wasn't over. James would pay, but first... Sirius needed to save them. And when the time came, he would make James regret every decision that had led to this moment. With his life.
